title: Implement Linux Mint local bootstrap and runtime roots
verify: Bash bootstrap creates or reuses .venv, installs project/test dependencies, and prepares .env from .env.example without printing secrets.
Settings expose local runtime roots for data/artifacts, timeline placeholder, temp/smoke paths, and local_only defaults.
Bootstrap gives actionable safe errors when Python or PostgreSQL tooling is missing on Linux Mint.

verify.summary: PostgreSQL client tooling is installed and detected; dry-run and full Linux Mint bootstrap passed without printing .env contents or credential-bearing DB URLs; bootstrap contract tests passed with 5 tests; baseline/database harness tests passed with 10 tests; mb-lint, mb-doctor, and git diff --check passed. Full T2 protocol and required packet/spec gates are satisfied.

evidence_required: bootstrap command transcript or documented dry-run evidence with secrets redacted
constraints: Do not require Docker or hosted services.
Do not print .env contents, passwords, tokens, or DB URLs with credentials.
Do not implement product domain behavior.
invariants: MVP remains local-first and private by default.
sync.status remains local_only until a future server-sync spec exists.
Secrets/auth material must not enter logs, exports, screenshots, Bus, UI Feed, or agent context.
purpose: Provide a repeatable Linux Mint local setup and runtime-root baseline for later backend feature tasks.
success_outcome: A Linux Mint operator can bootstrap the local backend environment and product tasks can rely on shared local runtime settings.
anti_goals: No product auth/session or UI implementation.

forbidden_scope: agent runtime, Safety Gate, photo catalog, timeline taxonomy, dataset governance, PWA UI
stop_conditions: Linux Mint bootstrap cannot be specified without leaking secrets.
Required local PostgreSQL assumptions are unclear or contradict .env.example.
